envelope.summary: Fetched and fully read the OpenAPI 3.0.3 description for the "Canary inventory/order service" at http://localhost:4100/openapi.json and confirmed it with read-only GETs only (no POSTs, no writes). Established the order contract (POST /orders, body {productId:string, qty:int>=1}, 201/409), stock read endpoints (GET /products paginated, GET /products/{id}), the reset/seed endpoint (POST /reset with optional per-product stock override), absence of auth, and the documented oversell rules ("stock never goes below zero", 409 Insufficient stock, cancel returns qty). Two surprises recorded: the paginated product list reports total=7 but returns only 6 items (p7 exists via GET /products/p7 yet appears on no page, contradicting "Every product appears on exactly one page"), and every response carries an undocumented `x-consistency: sync` header.
envelope.test_strength: Read-only interface exploration: 1 spec fetch + ~20 GET/HEAD requests across /health, /products (multiple page/size combos), /products/{id} (hit + miss), /orders, /coupons/{code} (hit + miss). No writes, no concurrency exercised.

claims.statement: Order placement is POST /orders with JSON body {productId: string (required), qty: integer minimum 1 (required)}; responses are 201 with an Order {id:string, productId:string, qty:integer, status:'placed'|'cancelled'} or 409 'Insufficient stock'.

Stock is read via GET /products (paginated: query page>=1 default 1, size 1..100 default 3; returns ProductPage {items, page, size, total, pages}) and GET /products/{id} (returns Product {id,name,price,stock}; 404 when missing).
A reset/seed endpoint exists: POST /reset with optional body {stock: {<productId>: integer}} to override stock per product id, resetting all state to seed data; no response schema is documented.

The spec declares no securitySchemes and no operation-level security, and unauthenticated GETs to /products, /products/{id}, /orders and /coupons/{code} all returned 200/404 without any credentials, so the API appears to require no authentication.

Documented stock/oversell rules: POST /orders 'Stock is decremented by qty; stock never goes below zero' with 409 for insufficient stock; POST /orders/{id}/cancel returns the order's qty to stock (200, 404 unknown, 409 already cancelled); POST /coupons/{code}/claim claims one use and 'remaining never goes below zero' (201, 409 quota exhausted).

The spec documents no idempotency mechanism (no idempotency-key header, no request-id, no dedup field), so each accepted POST /orders must be assumed to decrement stock exactly once with no documented duplicate suppression.

GET /products is internally inconsistent with GET /products/{id}: total=7 is reported and pages=3 for size=3, yet pages 1..3 return only p1..p6 (p3 empty) and size=100 returns only 6 items, while GET /products/p7 returns 200 {id:'p7',name:'Whatsit',price:3.3,stock:40} — so p7 appears on no page, contradicting the documented 'Every product appears on exactly one page'.
claims.minimal_repro: curl -s 'http://localhost:4100/products?page=1&size=100' | grep -o '"id":"p[0-9]*"'  # 6 ids; then curl -s http://localhost:4100/products/p7  # 200

claims.statement: All responses carry an undocumented response header `x-consistency: sync`, suggesting the SUT advertises synchronous (non-eventual) stock consistency; no `Server` header is emitted, so the runtime stack could not be identified.

Seed data observed read-only: p1 Widget price 9.5 stock 10, p2 Gadget price 19 stock 5, p3 Doohickey price 4.25 stock 100, p4 Sprocket price 1.1 stock 25, p5 Gizmo price 42 stock 3, p6 Thingamajig price 7 stock 12, p7 Whatsit price 3.3 stock 40; coupon SAVE10 {quota:5, remaining:5}; GET /orders returns {"items":[]}. Small-stock targets for an oversell test are p5 (3) and p2 (5).

Coverage gap: only GET/HEAD requests were issued (strict read-only mandate); POST /orders, POST /orders/{id}/cancel, POST /reset and POST /coupons/{code}/claim were never exercised, so their runtime behaviour (including whether oversell actually occurs) is unverified and left to the executor mission.

Unknown-route behaviour is uniform: GET /, GET /docs, GET /api/orders, GET /orders/abc, GET /products/does-not-exist and GET /coupons/<unknown> all return JSON {"error":"..."} with 404, and OPTIONS /orders and OPTIONS /reset return 404 (no CORS preflight support).

envelope.summary: POST /orders oversells under concurrency, deterministically and severely. Seeding p2=5 and firing 20 simultaneous qty-1 orders returns 20x201 / 0x409 and leaves stock at 4, so 20 units are sold from a 5-unit stock and the final stock never falls below 4 (delta 4 regardless of N). Reproduced 6/6 by two independent load generators (Python raw sockets, curl --parallel) and in every node-harness run, on 3 products, with qty 1 and 2 and mixed qty, while the sequential control (5x201/20x409, final 0) shows the spec is satisfiable and the defect is concurrency-specific. Cancel paths behave correctly (single cancel under 10 simultaneous cancels), so the fault is confined to order placement's check-then-decrement.

envelope.summary: Built and registered the `http-burst-client` skill (candidate provider for cap:http-client, hash 647a64c4) under quarantine/http-burst-client. It wraps Node's core http/https modules with an explicit keep-alive Agent: a warm-up pre-opens N sockets, then N requests are issued as one simultaneous burst (all request promises created and written before any response is awaited) or sequentially, returning per-request status, status message, HTTP version, headers, verbatim raw body text, durationMs, issuedOffsetMs/respondedOffsetMs and a connection-reuse flag as one JSON object. skill_validate passes clean and a local smoke run over the mechanics/JSON contract passed; I did not judge the SUT.

claims.statement: Registered candidate provider http-burst-client@0.1.0 (hash 647a64c4) for cap:http-client; skill_validate reports ok and the skill directory quarantines cleanly with hosts=[localhost:4100], no writes and no exec.

The provider's own mechanics and JSON contract work: single GET returns status/headers/raw body/duration, an 8-request burst pre-opens 8 keep-alive sockets and reports allIssuedBeforeFirstResponse=true with every request on a pooled socket, a 409 is returned verbatim as data with error=null, sequential mode is correctly not simultaneous, and a missing --base exits 2.

Acceptance hint probe: `node scripts/burst.mjs --base http://localhost:4100 --path "/products/p1"` returns raw body {"id":"p1","name":"Widget","price":9.5,"stock":10}, i.e. the provider surfaces the stock field verbatim; no judgement about the SUT is made here.

capability_issues: No hard-coded hosts by design: the base URL is a required --base argument, so any caller must pass the SUT origin explicitly.

Git-Bash/MSYS shells rewrite an unquoted leading '/' in --path into a Windows path (e.g. C:/Program Files/PortableGit/...); callers must quote the value or set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1. The skill resolves paths against the base URL origin, so a stray absolute Windows path now fails as a 404 rather than silently hitting the wrong route, but the shell-level quoting requirement remains.

Timing fields are millisecond-resolution wall-clock offsets measured in the client process; the skill cannot measure server-side queueing separately, and 'simultaneous' is reported as evidence (allIssuedBeforeFirstResponse, issuedSpanMs) rather than enforced.
No HTTP/2 or raw-socket mode; the provider is HTTP/1.1 keep-alive over the Node agent, and TLS is supported only via --insecure flag (no custom CA bundle option).

claims.statement: Registered provider http-burst@b54f8405 (kind skill, path quarantine/http-burst, cap:concurrency) fills the gap: it pre-establishes all N connections, then releases every raw HTTP/1.1 request from one synchronous write loop, returning responses in request order with burst start/end timestamps and per-request write offsets.

The burst is tight enough to exercise a race deterministically: with 60 pre-connected sockets the last write offset stays under 3 ms, a racy mock server reliably reports 60 successes against stock=5, and an atomic mock server caps successes at exactly 5 with 55 rejections.
All 50 simultaneously issued GETs to the mission target http://localhost:4100/products were collected with HTTP 200, parsed JSON bodies, and per-request write offset/first-byte/latency timings.

capability_issues: cap:concurrency is provided for HTTP/1.1 only. HTTP/2 multiplexing (many concurrent streams over a single connection, where the server sees them in one connection rather than N sockets) is not supported; --insecure/--keep-alive exist but there is no h2 client.

No cross-process burst coordination primitive beyond --release-at <epoch-ms> (absolute wall-clock release). Sub-millisecond agreement between independently launched processes is not achievable, so a single process must own the whole burst.

The provider has no built-in assertion layer: it returns timings, status counts and extracted JSON fields, but deciding whether a given status histogram is a defect (e.g. oversell detection against known stock) is left to the caller.

Windows POSIX-shell path rewriting (Git Bash/MSYS) silently mangles a leading-slash --path; the provider detects and repairs the common install-root shape, but a custom MSYS root would still need the --path=<relative> equals form or MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1.

deviations.agent_hypothesis: A single --path argument would work identically across shells.
deviations.observed: Git Bash/MSYS rewrote the argument to /C:/Program Files/PortableGit/products, producing 50x HTTP 400; added shell-rewrite detection with recovery plus SKILL.md guidance and re-registered.

envelope.summary: Curator mission for i-20261026-8dad24 ran out of budget before template_propose could be called; no draft template id was minted. I read the episode report, the frozen burst harness (t1_oversell_burst.mjs), lib/http.mjs and lib/oracle.mjs to extract the reusable method: seed a shared resource via a reset/override endpoint, warm up pre-opened keep-alive sockets, release N requests as one simultaneous burst, then assert the spec invariant "accepted quantity <= seeded amount and stored resource == seed - accepted" plus a sequential control. That method (and its known pitfalls: timing-sensitive load generators, global reset state, cross-mission interference) is recorded here so a follow-up curator run can propose the template from it.

claims.statement: The distilled method for this class of test is: read the spec's conservation rule for a shared resource, seed a small amount through the reset/override endpoint, verify the seed read-back as a precondition, warm up N pre-opened keep-alive sockets, release N requests in one simultaneous burst (all promises created before any await), then assert (a) accepted quantity <= seeded amount, (b) stored resource == seed - accepted, (c) statuses only from the documented set, and (d) a sequential control with the same requests yields exactly the documented accept/reject split.

Known pitfalls to carry into the template: per-process TCP handshakes (N separate curl processes) stagger the burst and produce a false negative; a global reset endpoint resets all resources so experiments must run strictly serially; appending `; echo $?` masks the script's exit code and flips the recorded verdict to pass; and a load-generator bug (e.g. curl -K body merging) can produce a false violation.
No template id was produced: template_propose was never reached because the mission budget was exhausted while reading the episode artefacts.

capability_issues: Episode evidence records that the environment template advertised cap:http-client and cap:concurrency but both were marked NOT AVAILABLE, so the executor had to implement the keep-alive HTTP burst client and the simultaneous-burst primitive by hand — a template for this test kind should require a burst-capable HTTP client capability.

deviations.expected: Call template_propose once to mint a draft strategy template, then finish with mission_submit.
deviations.observed: Budget was exhausted during artefact reading (report + frozen harness/oracle/http libs); template_propose was never called, so no draft template exists and the distilled method is reported in the claim text instead.
